limits_note: The question in the brief was whether any of these expose an HTTP egress endpoint. Answer: no. Every one of them is a supply-side client whose traffic is sold wholesale to a proxy network, and the buyer-side products are sold by the network (Bright Data, IPRoyal, PacketStream, Proxyrack), not by the app. The arbitrage of signing up as a contributor on one and consuming on another does not exist either, because the spread is 10x-45x and the contributor is paid in cash, capped per IP.
reliability_note: Per-IP caps and per-IP demand make earnings non-scalable; Honeygain's own example needs three separate networks to reach $5-6.67/month; Emerging Threats now ships 'ADWARE_PUP: Bandwidth Sharing Tool' rules for 5 of these 8 domains, so IDS-equipped networks flag them.

extras.agent_focus: Marketplaces and networks where storage or bandwidth is contributed by third parties for free or near-free. Two directions probed: (1) BUY side - can you consume contributed bandwidth/storage cheaply; (2) SUPPLY side - the arbitrage question, whether contributing a disk earns storage credit at better than the retail rate. Also research testbeds that hand out whole physical nodes with multi-TB local disk (CloudLab, Chameleon, FABRIC, Emulab) and community mesh networks (Guifi, Freifunk, NYC Mesh). Decided per candidate by computing 20 TiB stored + 1 TiB/day egress against that path's actual tariff.
